utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in the courtroom. We are now sitting in Courtroom I; it's quite unusual, but it was because of our time change, and I hope, Mr. Tolimir, that was a good day for you this morning. Is the next witness ready?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I'm told that he is in the waiting room, which I am not sure, I don't recall where it is here, but hopefully close by.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You are not used to sit in this courtroom, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's been a while. We have made a tour of all the courtrooms, but having Ms. Stewart on my left is very strange, but we'll get used to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Welcome to the Tribunal. Would you please read aloud the solemn declaration which is shown to you on the card now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sit down, please. Mr. McCloskey has some questions for you, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, can you first tell us your name.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: My name is Jean-Rene Ruez.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Mr. Ruez, can you tell us, was there a time when you were the lead -- the team leader for the Srebrenica team here at the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I was a member of the Tribunal from April 1995 through April 2001. I started to work on the Srebrenica investigation just after events happened in July 1995. At that time I was an investigator within the team investigating the seizure of Sarajevo, but after that, I did only that, and I became investigation team leader at the beginning of 2007 when at last an investigation team was set up for this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think you said 2007 --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: 1997, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Right. Okay. And can you tell us, let's just go to the present, what is your current position?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I'm chief superintendent in French National Police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you tell us anything about your current assignment?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. I'm -- my previous assignments prior to joining the Tribunal was adding services working in the field of judicial police, and at this time I'm police attache in a French embassy abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask you to take short pauses between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And of course, we all notice you are speaking English. Is that your choice?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it is my choice indeed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, can you give us a bit about your educational background and how it was that you ended up becoming a member of the judicial police as a career. Just briefly.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: After finalising my university studies I passed a contest that allowed me to join the national police directly at the rank of superintendent, and I chose the option to work in the field of judicial police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And does that involve a law degree in your educational background?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you've spoken a little bit about your job from 1995 to 2006 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, 2001, we'll get our years right. Your six years as the team leader for Srebrenica mostly. Can you tell us just a little bit about your job there as an investigator and then we'll get right into the details of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: To make it very short, this investigation could be sliced into layers that happened when time was evolutioning. So at the beginning the main task was to compile witness testimonies, then to interview these witnesses, identify the locations where they were talking about. Once the possibility was open go to the Republika Srpska area and find these places, check what could match or not match in order to implement or not to implement the witness testimonies. After that was the need to find the bodies, so to identify, locate, and have primary mass graves exhumed. Following this was the need to find documentation and various materials that could help understand a broader picture of this case. And at the final stage was the task to interview those we believed had things that could enable to have the truth come out of it, so mainly the arrest army personnel, but also police personnel, civilian personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And you have testified the Krstic case, the Blagojevic case and the Popovic case for the Prosecution in this regard, have you not?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Among others, yes, those were on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And have you assembled your own group of photographs and videos and maps as part of that testimony?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I would assess that 80 per cent of what we present is my material indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And did you make a book for the Popovic case that you had a chance to review for this particular trial?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And can you just briefly tell us what that book entailed?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The book is designed to help those who have not been on the ground to visualise the chronology of the events that unfolded from the 11 July through 17 July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So I think as we have before, we'll go right to that book, which is 65 ter 1450.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be on e-court, of course, page by page, and the general has a B/C/S version that we've given him in hard copy. We also have hard copies for the Court, if you would like, we can pass out at the break. But of course, everything is on the computer, and we will just endeavour to go through that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Ruez, let's start hopefully with page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we move this over so Ms. Stewart can do it. I think we are pretty well practiced at Sanction, so it might be a little easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I've got your outline in front of me, your -- basically your table of contents which begins with a map of the general area, which is actually page 5. And is this a map that you drew up?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: There is maybe a switch somewhere to go from text to picture, if I remember where now. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And we -- do you see that -- that map, we see Zeleni Jadar in the south and up to Kula Branjevo in the north?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This map is the global map of the entire crime scene area, so from south, indeed, to Zeleni Jadar up to north which is the Branjevo farm, Pilica village, and the blue box is roughly the Srebrenica safe area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And Srebrenica was the first part of your chapter. Let's go to page 6, the next page. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is a view of Srebrenica town as seen from the south. So in order to see it's a town stretched in between two hills, and the area south is the area from which VRS entered the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next one, 7.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Same reason for this picture. In order to give a visual of how this town is constructed, stretched in between two hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We see what I believe is part of a helicopter. Did you take these photographs?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall when you did?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That was probably in 1998. It was a helicopter mission in preparation of visuals for the sake of the trial of General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next shot. What is this map graphic? It's number 8.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this one is to indicate that on 11 July the population within the safe area took two directions of -- two courses of action. Via 28 division, so the army, the Bosnian army, as well as most of the able men took the decision to gather at an area the north of the enclave named Susnjari in order to abandon the -- the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us, we see kind of a grey outline with little yellow letters, what is that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The grey outline is the rough border, if one can say so, because there was no border line, but it's the limits of the so-called safe area. And the little dots with letters are the observation posts set up by the UN force that was protecting the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And this green arrow, I think you've already said, is -- what is that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The direction of movement of those who decided to flee the enclave in the 11 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to page 9. And we see about the same photograph but with a blue arrow and a blue circle. What is the significance of this dot?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is the second movement, the population the safe haven took, that is all the women, the elderly, the children, and an unknown number of men who decided not to flee the enclave but to find refuge at the main UN base that was in Potocari. So they had a stretch of road of a few kilometres to walk in order to find shelter at the main UN base of Srebrenica safe area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we see the scale that this is 5 kilometres, so that puts -- each one of these squares is 1 kilometre; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this map is to scale?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So let's go to page 10. Now, this is a very particular-looking black and white photograph. Can you explain what this product represent? What is it and what does the material on it mean?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This picture is a picture taken by a US aerial reconnaissance platform dated 13 July 1995. What is written in black over blank is the product provided by the US State Department, and all the indications in yellow are markings that I added to the picture in order to pin-point some locations in Potocari that have been of interest during the 12 and the 13 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, as you may be aware, the Trial Chamber has heard a few witnesses already. They heard some evidence about a house where men were taken to. Was there such a house in your investigation that you were able to identify?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is that noted here?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It is the circle of written "White House" knowing prior to that, that most of the refugees were at the north of this picture in mainly three places that were at the left: Express Bus compound, on the right; Energoinvest factory, the so-called "11 of March factory;" and also the zinc factory. These were the main spots the refugees were trying to find shelter. These places were overcrowded, so in fact there were refugees everywhere, except in the location labelled "blue factory" that was used by Bosnian Serb army. But they were also in the main base, in the UN base, approximately 5.000 refugees who were --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: The speakers are kindly asked to slow down and pause between questions and answers. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So I repeat. In the UN base also were approximately 5.000 refugees hiding inside. The relevance of the "White House" is that just a bit above the "White House" was a line of soldiers, first a line of UN soldiers and then a line of Bosnian Serb soldiers, and at the time the refugees were supposed to get on board of buses. This is where they were separated from their families, and these prisoners were systematically taken to the so-called "White House."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next page, page 11. And is this another photograph you took or someone else?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: No, this is a photograph that I took. It's another view of the previous photograph but seen from south to north. So opposite direction. And in the blue circle is the UN base, and the "White House" is in the white circle, so it shows the distance between the two locations, and the road that goes from the bottom to the picture to the north of the picture is the road that goes to Bratunac town. That was the destination of the prisoners who were inside the "White House."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And is this another photograph you took from a helicopter?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to page 12. Now, before we get into this picture, can you tell us when the first time about that you were able to go to this region after these crimes were reported in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The first time is the date of this picture, and that was January or February, February, I think, 2006, is so this is why it's winter-time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry, we are doing that again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: 1996, okay. It's getting to be awhile back.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: But the reason why I used this one is because it is the freshest in between July 1995 and the first time we approached this place, so for sure there was no snow in summer 1995. It was a very warm summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next shot. And we see the same "White House." Can you tell us what the significance of this two-part picture is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. The picture above is a still extracted from a videotape taken by a Serb journalist, propagandist named Zoran Petrovic, who did cut out from his original footage some pictures that could be embarrassing for the Bosnian Serb army. And on the picture at the top, which is an extract from his film, one can see a man sitting on a balcony. And this balcony is the first floor of the "White House," the house that all the witnesses say was the storage place for the prisoners that were then -- when they are shipped to Bratunac. And it is also a house that was visited by a Kenyan UN military observer who was present in Potocari, Major Kingori, who could enter the place and witnessed that it was packed with people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: As I mentioned to you, we are not going to play the -- what we call, the trial video for you. We've been able to, I think, save some time. But can you explain to us a little bit more about the Petrovic film and the two different versions of it. When -- let's start out, when did Petrovic -- do you know what day it was that he actually did this film or he filmed the people we are seeing right now?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I don't know for sure how many days he did spend in the area, but we know for sure that some of his footages are dated 13 July, so this one, if he was not there a day before, should be dated 13 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And when did the -- as far as you know, well, yourself first become aware of this footage that actually had men on the balcony? Just roughly.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I think this was in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And the original Petrovic film that was obtained by the Office of the Prosecutor, do you know when roughly when the in the investigation that was obtained?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I think we obtained it from a different channel more or less at the same time in 2001. I was no longer at the Tribunal, but someone came to see me to show it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And the video that had this material edited out of it, had that been in the investigation for a long time prior to this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Sure, because the public part of the film is something that we worked on frame by frame, mainly in order to identify people, the arrest personnel, but mainly men who appeared on the film and that we tried to find and only to find out that they were missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you tell us -- we see this little circle, and it's barely readable up in the right-hand corner of the black and white picture. Can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it is the Logo of Studio B, that is a Serbian dependant -- so-called independent TV station.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what does that have to do with this story? Do you recall how it was that there was a Studio B logo on this other footage?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Because the journalist who shot this film was on the staff, and he was working for this TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right, and we will get into some other photographs where we see additional Studio B sections of this video a little bit later. All right. Now, let's go to the next page which is page 14. We have a new map. What does this symbolise? Where are we going now in your presentation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Once the house, the "White House," was filled with prisoners, it had to be emptied. The men on board -- in the house were taken on board of buses, and driven towards the town nearby, that is Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now let's go to 15. Now, tell us what this is.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So again this is an aerial imagery of Bratunac town dated 12 July, and this picture shows the first location where a man who had been previously taken to the "White House" were eventually transported to the centre of this town at the location named "the hangar." And this hangar is, in fact, just behind the main school of the town that is named Vuk Karadzic school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to page 17. And what is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a ground view of this hangar that was first a detention place used in Bratunac town, aside another one that we learned later on about, that was the soccer field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to page 18. Now we have a new diagram and a letter -- excuse me, an arrow going from Jaglici Susnjari area towards Konjevic Polje and Cerska. What is this symbolising?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This second arrow symbolises the direction that all those who did gather in the Susnjari area took during the night between the 11 and the 12 and during the day of the 12, so hitting the direction of north-west, trying to reach this strategic intersection that is Konjevic Polje and then move towards the north in order to try to reach the Bosnian lines in the vicinity of Nezuk, in the north-west of this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just very roughly, what kind of terrain would they be covering as they left the Jaglici Susnjari village area?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It is a hilly terrain that goes along asphalt road, and the direction to be taken for those who were not at all from this area who were refugees who had ended up at the early months of the war in this Srebrenica area was to follow a line of pylons that were running on a hill that is just above the asphalt road going from Bratunac towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Go to page 19. What does this photograph depict?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So at the bottom you can see the asphalt road I was just talking about, then the hill. And, in fact, the column was walking like an ant column just behind the top of this hill, so that they could not be seen from the asphalt road. And that's the type of terrain they were walking through.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to page 20. What is this? This one photograph put together, I guess, with two.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It's in fact three even. This is in order to indicate what was the end point of this first part of the journey that was in fact a big hill overlooking the Konjevic Polje intersection, going then -- in one direction would go towards Nova Kasaba, a place we'll talk about later. And so this is the area of intersection of Konjevic Polje. From the top of this hill, those who intended to cross could have a good look on the area, so to find the best moment they could try to cross, or also a place from where they could see events, we will talk about also later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next photograph, 21.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is another view of the direction they were willing to take, and in order to take this direction, via the yellow arrow, there was still the need to cross the asphalt road. At the end of 12 July, the 28 Division who was at the spear-head of this column of people succeeded going through this place, but the following day all this area was cordoned off by Bosnian Serb army and people -- very few people could succeed crossing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, this little cluster of buildings we see on the right side, what is the name of that little area?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is the village of Konjevici, which is another name for Konjevic Polje; it's the same thing. Konjevici and Konjevic Polje is this intersection, in fact. Going north up to the picture towards Zvornik and to the left towards Nova Kasaba, the asphalt road that would hit to the right would be the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's go to page 22, and we have a section that you've entitled "prisoners of war, regroupment sites, 13 July." What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: After the night 12/13 July, all the people who were still in this area and did not manage to cross the night before were trapped in this place, and they were led to surrender by people on the asphalt road wearing blue helmets and shouting them that they should surrender, that the UN was there, that the HCR was there, that they would be reunited soon with their families. So all this sparked a massive movement of surrender. If we start with completely the left side, this surrender spot which is close to -- it's not a surrender spot; in reality, it's a separation spot. For those who had been -- who managed on the 12 to get on board of buses, there was a second line of screening of people before allowing them to cross the line to Kladanj, so they were separated at a location named Luke where there is a little school where they would be put in. And all the other spots, one we already talked about is the "White House" in Potocari, Bratunac, also we talked about it. And then there are the main spots in the middle of the map which are the spots close to this end of the map at Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And early on in the investigation as you learned about these places, did you go to each one of them individually?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, yes. As soon as 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And let's go to page 24, then, and can you -- do you recognise what this photograph or series of photographs is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is the elementary school of Luke. The buses coming from Bratunac were taking this road, and at approximately 500 metres away from this school was a parking-lot, and then started the separation line with -- between Republika Srpska and the Bosniak side of the territory. And the men who were spotted on board of these buses were taken back along this road and put in this elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how did you find that school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It took a little while because initially we spotted Luke in a place inside Vlasenica town, but then moving back and forth along this stretch of road going to Kladanj, we spotted this school and ended up realising this was the good one, and we later on brought on the spot one man who had been kept prisoner inside this school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to page 25. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is a photograph taken from the back of the school, and the trees is the area where some of the prisoners were taken and sitting there. This is a picture I took on the indication of the former prisoner who explained the setup of how the prisoners were kept there. So in between -- under these trees was a group, and then he was taken inside the classroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to page 26. What is the significance of this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is the classroom where this witness -- that this witness recognised as being the one he had been kept inside and where he was subsequently also beaten up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next segment. This is at page 27, again a map we are familiar with. What is this signifying?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is again spots of concentration spots for prisoners in the vicinity of Nova Kasaba and -- Nova Kasaba mainly for this one, Nova Kasaba concentration spots. Two areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to page 28 for a better picture. Now, is this one of these aerial images provided by the United States that you've been talking about?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And have you relied on this information in black or yellow or both? Can you explain that again just briefly.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this picture is US provided. The markings in yellow are the ones that I have added. The building at the bottom of the picture is the 65th Protection Regiment designed for the protection of General Mladic, and that is located here in Nova Kasaba. And in front of it one can see three buses parked in front of this military facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to page 29. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is the same building but seen from the asphalt road that goes from Nova Kasaba towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to page 30. Now, we see this is still Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is an area a few k away at the north from the 65th Protection Regiment. It's a soccer field of Nova Kasaba. And those who were on this big hill we showed previously, this was their main spot for surrendering. They went downhill, and they were regrouped on the soccer field that is just underneath the white band marked "Bus Convoy." That's the soccer field. The next photo will show my own markings of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to that photograph, then, 31.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this indicates the soccer field and areas that show groups of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, we noted -- how do you know that those are groups of prisoners? Why do you conclude that? We obviously from this level can't tell that.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: We have another one with a closer shot, and we had one labelled as such. And I also, I mean, we also talked with witnesses who were driving towards the confrontation line on board of these buses who could testify these were witnesses -- sorry, these were prisoners. And I also talked about, off record, with someone who was on this soccer field registering people in the early hours of this process, but then they quickly stopped registering people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. I failed to ask you, but on the last photograph which had the same thing, it says "13 July 1995," and then a squiggly line, "1400 hours." Now, as we've learned, this black and white information was provided by the United States. What is that squiggly line, "1400 hours" mean? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It means approximately 1400 hours, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next photograph, 32. Is this what you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, even in addition to what I said, it's the analysis of those who did the imagery analysis to conclude that, indeed, we are talking about people on this soccer field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When you say those that did it, are you talking about the United States provider?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 33. What is the significance of this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is to give a feeling of the size of the area in order to have a better estimate of a linkage between the area reconnaissance imagery and the picture taken from a helicopter from above.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I interrupt you for a short moment. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to object. For 20 minutes now we've been looking at photographs which have been selected by an unknown person, one-sidedly, and all we see on them are facts that would be in favour of the Prosecution. If the aerial photographs were made, they would have been made, and they should have depicted everything. We couldn't see that column of 10 kilometres long, and it's not possible that such an aerial photo was taken and that you wouldn't see such a column. So we should see here photographs that would actually show us the true events and how this column moved, where it went, and so on. So I would really appreciate it if you could now seek answers to all these questions and that these photos not be used until you get answers to these questions so that whatever we learn here could be in the interest of both the Prosecution and the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, your comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would briefly state that these -- yes, these are materials chosen by Mr. Ruez, and of course, the General is free to cross-examine Mr. Ruez on any such points, though, I can also say that I did not believe that the numbers in the path of the column was an item that was in dispute at all, but he is certainly open to cross-examine Mr. Ruez and determine what other materials are available. We are, of course, always ready to answer his questions should he want pictures of individual items. In fact, the United States remains open for his requests of this kind of aerial imagery as they are to the -- both the Prosecution and the Defence. So he is free to request to the United States any potential imagery of the column. We are not free under our Rule 70 restrictions to comment on what may or may not be out there in terms of United States aerial imagery, unless it has been, in particularly, provided authority to use, which many of these have been for years. But Mr. Ruez will not, as he well knows, be able to answer questions about what else may be out there. But the General is free to ask the United States, and he may not know that, and so I -- in thinking about it, it's good that he knows that, if that's something that he is interested in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, I think it's very clear that you have the right during your cross-examination, after the examination-in-chief, to raise all your concerns and to put the relevant questions to this witness. Thank you. Please carry on, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So, Mr. Ruez, just to be clear, is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I think Mr. Tolimir would like to raise another problem. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to point out the problem of conducting investigations. This Prosecution was supposed to investigate matters, and just as he showed the photos, the aerial photos that we've seen here, they should also have shown the photos depicting the Baljkovica, where the fighting was going on, where the column was, and so on. Why should I seek those photos? This was also mentioned earlier in other cases where the Defence could seek such aerial photos from the United States, but this was suggested earlier, and, actually, the Defence was never able to obtain any such documents from the United States. So perhaps the Trial Chamber could seek to obtain such documents, because this would be in the interests of justice and determination of the truth. You should establish the truth, whether this column was a military column or a civilian column. Why don't we have this information? Did the American intelligence service only provide the imagery that would be in favour of one side in these proceedings? And I would really appreciate getting answers to these photos. And pending answers to all these questions, I would seek that these photos not be used because they are -- this selection is only of photos that are in favour of the Prosecution case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you got already the answer of the Chamber. You may deal with these problems during your cross-examination. The moment is the Prosecution who is putting questions to the witness related to these photos the witness can give information about. And for your question how to find out the truth, this is, at the end, the task of the Chamber to find out and to give weight to the evidence. Please carry on, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, just to be clear, do we see the soccer pitch on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. This is designed to show what is the real vision of this field compared with this black and white seen-from-above aerial imagery we've seen before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we go towards the top of this picture, what direction are we going in, just to try to orient ourselves?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, the top is the direction of Nova Kasaba, and the bottom is the direction of Konjevic Polje. And the hill the prisoners were surrendering from is at the left side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you move to the next picture, a question from my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: I was waiting for the translation. [Interpretation] Witness, this is the soccer pitch next to the 65 Protection Regiment of General Mladic. Now, I don't know whether in line with the Prosecution's question you will come back to this photograph that we saw earlier where there were people on the soccer pitch, and you said that these people were prisoners. But it's quite blurry, and for the moment we can't really tell whether these are people or trucks or anything else. But more essentially, this group of people or trucks was extremely well organised, you know, in the middle of the soccer pitch, so it's a bit strange. I would like to know whether Mr. McCloskey or yourself would like to comment on this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not make a direct connection at all between the previous photograph showing the 65th Protection Regiment with three buses inside this compound with this picture of a football pitch of Nova Kasaba. The only goal at this stage is to show that at Nova Kasaba there were two regroupment pools of prisoners, one being the compound of the 65th Protection Regiment where the only thing the picture shows is the presence of three buses. We do not know if they are empty; we do not know if they are full. There are Dutch witnesses who were inside this compound and who can testify about the fact that this was a detention facility during these days. And the second separate situation is this football pitch where there are no buses on it, the buses we can see are the buses taking people from Potocari towards Kladanj, is the second and last day of the deportation of the population, and the fact, indeed, is that the people are well lined up. But as you will see in terms of organising the prisoners, these prisoners are always well lined up. We have other pictures show that this was an organised process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, I know it's been a long time. Do you recall any intercept from this time-period that has anything to do with this topic? And if not, we'll go on.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I would prefer not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And was there a military analyst in the team that discusses military documents, military facilities, intercepts, things like that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Sure, we have Stefanie Frease who will give any useful detail about the analysis of all what is intercepted communication, and Richard Butler who did the analysis of all the documents that we captured during the search of the Bratunac -- mainly the Bratunac and the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And these black and white conclusions on the United States aerial images, this one, you know, on page, well, 32, the previous page - if we could go back to that - how much faith did you have in the correctness of those conclusions?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: For me, it's a hundred per cent because I can even see the guards on this picture. I see one group in the middle, one stretch on the left and dots, which knowing the ground quite well, I spot them as being individuals, these dots.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And I think you said it, but is there in fact, one survivor witness that should be in evidence in this case to talk in more detail about this soccer pitch?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I remember very well a young pregnant woman I talked with during the summer 1995 and who was a prisoner on this field before being put on board of a bus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, may I interrupt very short. There are two questions. My question is, if I understood it correctly what the witness said, you asked the witness line 11, on page 23, "Do you recall intercept?" And the witness answered, "I would prefer not." I would kindly ask to clarify that. Do you recall or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't recall. I recall we have something in connection with this location, but I don't remember precisely what, and I'm not the one usually talking about the analysis of intercepts. This is why I prefer to stick on my role. I was not the analyst of all these intercepts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. That clarifies the situation. Judge Nyambe has a question to that photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Yes, I think page 24, line 3 to 5, you have just said, "I see one group in the middle, one stretch on the" -- I've lost that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: "I spot them as being individuals, these dots." Can you please mark those individuals on the picture.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I had an arrow, I could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Is it possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you see the big square, let's say, the rectangle in the middle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps we can have it on the screen with -- in another format so that it could be marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I am sorry, if we could flip into e-court, then he could mark it with the pen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How does this work? Can one erase these markings that were done not on purpose. Okay. Let's erase. Okay, so this is one group of people; this is another group of people. But here, it's one individual; here one individual, one individual, one. And maybe one or two, I don't know because it's fuzzy. But as you will see on another picture, there are no bushes on this picture. And these individual dots - but we will have others on other pictures - for me, I identify them as individuals. So, for me, these dots here are guards, as well as this ones. These ones sitting altogether are the prisoners. Sitting or standing, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we would offer - we'll get a number for us - this into evidence. And 1450, page 32, marked by Witness Ruez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have on channel 4, the French translation. I think Judge Nyambe didn't finish, and then after that Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do I understand you to say by looking at this picture you are able to say there were people there? There are people there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For me, as long as this picture is labelled as a representing people, the locations where these people are assembled when I look at this picture is exactly the ones I just marked, a large group in the middle, another group stretched on the side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Your Honour, the witness said that he thinks these are people. Did he hear this from those who analysed these images, or does he see it and we do not? Anyone can shadow in a certain surface and say that these are people. But if you look at the bushes, the shadows look similar to this square marked by the witness, so can he tell us whether that's his personal opinion? He said he thought. Does he think that, or did he hear from someone, or was he told by someone who was interpreting images for him? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, this is not the right moment to put questions to the witness from your side. At the moment we are in the examination-in-chief. You should note that question and come back to that during your cross-examination. And then you will have the chance to see this photo again. This photo with the markings, I hope we didn't lose them, will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P77, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just so -- I want to be clear on Judge Nyambe's question. Is there -- when you have -- are of the opinion that these are people, are you using anything besides this photograph to come to that opinion, or are you just using solely this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I use, in fact, and I will answer in advance to the question of General Tolimir that he will put to me in cross, I also use the fact that I have spent numerous and numerous hours analysing all these pictures and identifying what reference they can have on the ground. So an example you will see also another photograph of this football pitch, that one can see there is no tree in the middle. It's a football field. There are no bushes in the middle. So these grey zones are not shadows. Though, indeed, a shadow has the same pixel than a group of people on the picture, but if you compare what is officially said on the photograph and the corroboration you can make of what a man represents in terms of a pixel on such a photo, this is why I allow myself to say that the dots that I have marked previously are people. And since they are not within the group of prisoners, my conclusion is that they are guards. Only the guards could be out of the area where the prisoners were to be sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Is it fair to say that there will be other evidence in this case on this point that the Court will view that you are privy to but we won't get into today?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Sure. You have in your back-pack many witnesses who can confirm that that day there were people on the soccer field of Nova Kasaba. I don't doubt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next -- well, let's go to 34. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a picture of the same soccer field dated April 1996, so a bit less than the date -- less than a year than the aerial photograph shows. And this gives an idea of the size of an individual on this terrain, and you can also identify some of these structures, half destroyed structures of the football field at the top of the picture on the aerial one. These people were dog handlers from the 65th Protection Regiment who appeared at random to be on this field the first day of our first real mission in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Perhaps let's go back to the 32 -- well, it's all right. Let's keep going. Let's go on to the next chapter, I think we are okay, unless there's any other questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thirty-five would be the next topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is this about?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is another spot in this area where we could identify it was a location where prisoners were taken to, a collection point of prisoners, just at the intersection of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 36. Here we have an aerial image marked Konjevic Polje. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is an aerial photograph of the facility of the 5th Engineer unit. It's a building just very close by the intersection of Konjevic Polje where one witness will most certainly come to testify at one stage, declared he was initially taken to. He was also taken to a little house which is in the box at the upper left of this picture which was used by this unit as a little communication centre. The picture shows that at that date there were trucks parked just behind that. If fact, they were not trucks, they were bridge trucks parked behind it. So this was a military facility that was the first spot some prisoners were reaching this area at Konjevic Polje were taken to before being taken to a hangar that is just at the intersection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to page 37. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is a view from the ground of a previous aerial imagery, and that is the entrance of 5th Engineer Unit, and the little house guard at the left is the first spot where that prisoner was initially taken to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 38.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The second destination after having hit this 5th Protection Regiment -- no, engineer unit, sorry, facility was to be taken to a hangar at the intersection. The only picture we have of this hangar is this one. It was not taken for that sake, but this hangar was then destroyed in 1997, so after that, we never could have any picture of this place, and it is the only available picture of what the prisoner names a hangar just at the intersection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall what is currently at that intersection where this building used to be?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: There was a gas station, brand new gas station constructed there in -- it was in, I think, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just to orient us again, this blue arrow, what is in the direction -- well, the opposite direction of the way that arrow is pointing?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: At the right of this picture is the direction of Bratunac, but it mainly points at -- the 5th Engineer Unit is just very nearby at the right side of this arrow. So the prisoner and the others, they had to walk and reach this hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this road that winds up the valley going towards the top of the picture, where is that road going again?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So that's the road entering the canyon of the Drinjaca, and continuing in that direction is the direction of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, and then this -- the road going to the left is in what direction?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: To the left is the direction of the soccer field of Nova Kasaba and Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, let's go to 39. Now, we see military vehicles here. What is this of?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is to have a closer shot of the hangar I was talking about. This picture was taken, I took this picture in April 1996, but as I said, one year later approximately, this construction was totally destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And April of 1996, are you travelling with these military vehicles?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It was our escort indeed, yes. Part of the escort.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Why? Why did you have an escort?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Because all the crime scenes we were looking at were, what I call, in the garden of the Drina Corps, and even the general commanding the Drina Corps at the time was the same one there in July 1995. The only change was it was no more the Drina Corps, it was the 5th Corps. But all the individuals, all the police, all the army, whoever had had his hands in the events of summer 1995 were still, more or less, all of them in their positions in 1996 and in 1997 and the years after.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's now go to page 40. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is also a main spot for surrendering, but not for those who were completely at the west of the first part of the trip, so trapped on this huge hill, but those who had been, in fact, stopped in the area during the night between the 12 and the 13 and who decided to surrender quite massively in the morning of the 13 of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is the name of this area?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The main spot, there were a few others, but the main one is a meadow at the location named Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next photograph. What does this signify, number 41?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This picture is taken from the asphalt road going from Konjevic Polje towards Bratunac. Behind this hill is, in fact, the approach of Sandici. The interest of this picture is that this one appears in the film of Zoran Petrovic where he is filming groups of people on top of a hill who are in the surrendering process and where when a few minutes later one of the soldiers is saying that since this morning 5.000 people surrendered in this area. So that's precisely the location. It can be compared with the film of Zoran Petrovic, mainly with two elements, one is the electric pylon, and also at the right it's a place where he films people who appear one by one and who are in the surrender process there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe has a question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Yes. Earlier in your testimony, I think it's page 7, lines 5 to 7, you referred to this same person Petrovic, Zoran's film.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Is this the same film you are talking about even now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it's the same film, but this is a part that he did not eliminate from his original film. I think you have seen the full Zoran Petrovic video already, as far as I heard. So these pictures are, in fact, to help you compare what you could see on his film and spot the areas, identify where these areas are. And this one is just before arriving at Sandici and in the chronology of his film, as you know, after Sandici, he is arriving at Kravica, and all these places are interconnected. It's the same stretch of road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Let me try to make this a little clearer by skipping ahead with the trial video. We've left out a little bit that you may need to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, can you tell us, Zoran Petrovic filmed basically, well, two areas famous to this investigation on the 13th of July. What was the first area that we see in filming?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The first area of interest that we can see on his film is indeed Srebrenica and Potocari. The second of very high interest is this stretch of road between Konjevic Polje and Sandici, but mainly Sandici in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So could we go to page 40. And so can you just point out again, well, you don't need to symbol it, but we see the area -- the other area that you are talking about that he filmed that we have.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Potocari, inside the enclave. And also Srebrenica town, there are a few footages of Srebrenica town which ended up being of interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But the section of road that you were talking about, between which areas?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It's the area of Sandici, Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. As we see on this map; correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: At the right of the blue dot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And just while we are on that point, there -- as you've said there are two different versions of the film, one what you call the public version and then this Studio B version. Can you tell us again, so it's clear, why we have two. Or just identify that so this makes sense, because you'll see photographs on this point.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The simple reason is that from his original film, Mr. Petrovic eliminated three small parts which were hard evidence against the people he was travelling with in this area. If I'm precise, there is the view of the man sitting on the balcony, that implement the fact that, indeed, the white -- so-called "White House" was used as a storage place for prisoners who were then, bus after bus, taken to Bratunac. One other thing he took out was 30 millimetre anti-aircraft guns shooting on people in the forest. He had kept the previous images of these vehicles shooting from the road, but he had taken away the impacts on the trees in the forest. And the main piece is the pictures we will see, the 3-second footage at the Kravica warehouse where dead bodies can be seen at the Kravica warehouse. So these three seconds are the only live pictures of an execution in the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps. So this is the reason why he erased this evidence from his film.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now let's go to your next sequence in this, which is page 42. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is a view of the hill from where the people who were trying to flee the area started to move downhill along the path, that one can see at the right, in order to join the asphalt road. And it's a bit hard to recognise, but this is also the place where Zoran Petrovic was filming when he is filming the people who arrive at Sandici and walk next to a big two-storage house and then go to the meadow where they are kept prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall the person that he -- that Zoran Petrovic was with mostly, the senior officer?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, he was with Colonel Borovcanin that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So obviously, Your Honours, that was from another case, another trial, and we will be seeing more information on that, but not, of course, as much detail as we may have seen in that other trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, let's now go to page 43. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is a picture taken from the direction of the surrendering prisoners were taken, and they were so going up towards this house. And at the left of the house, that's where the film taken by Zoran Petrovic shows the Serb soldiers giving orders to the prisoners in order -- then behind this house is an asphalt road, and just after the asphalt road is the Sandici meadow, so that's the way. And in 1996 there were still a lot of abandon bags and so on at this location that were creating a trail that was, in fact, the trail taken by the people who were surrendering.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to page 44. Another American aerial image. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is, indeed, US material dated 13 July. The group of people will be visible on the next one because the next one has my markings. But on this one, what you can see, middle left there are buses on that location. One cannot see they are moving or not. And the trail is at the left, the top left of the picture, you can see the trail going down hitting the asphalt road, and more or less in the middle, but the next picture will indicate where the group of people is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 45 then, the next picture.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So the trail is the little line, the little line going from the top of the picture then goes along the destroyed house. That's the precise location where Zoran Petrovic was filming.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me for interrupting. This destroyed house, does that have any relationship to the partly destroyed house we just saw?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it's the one we saw on the previous two pictures before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: And the group of people is the one marked in a circle, group of people. And at the right I mark the destroyed houses because one of the -- one witness who was on this meadow said that the wounded were taken to the right towards destroyed houses, so that's the location where the destroyed houses are, but, I mean, we have no idea about the fate of these wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: One thing also, on this one it would be very hard to assess any kind of numbers based on this picture and the location of the group of prisoners because this picture is not straight from above. Is it taken into an angle, and this is a slope, and we are viewing the slope from top to bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. We'll get a little better picture. Let's go to 46. Now, again here we see the United States says group of people, Sandici, 13 July, approximately 1400 hours. Without going into your investigation, do you -- what is your opinion that this depicts?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: In my opinion it depicts what it says, what it says, what is written on it. We will have the possibility to check that with additional photos coming right after. But again, it's an interesting thing because we have -- we can see that it is taken -- it's a side shot; it's not a shot from above. One can see shadows of the buses, the roof and the shadows, so it gives them some volume. Same thing for the two-storage house; we can see it from the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. Can we just put this on e-court again. And if we can go to that last image, if you can find it. H46.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Mr. Ruez, if you could take that pen again and mark what you believe is the group of people.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is the group of people, but again, seen from a slope that goes from top to bottom. So in fact, these ones are hiding those who are in front of him, getting in a slope. So this is not the full length of that group. This picture, as you can see, is not taken from the top to bottom, but we can see the shadows of the buses here on the side. We can see the facade of the house, of this one house. So we have it from an angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned a witness told you that wounded were taken to some house. Do you see the area that he would have been telling you?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: There's one of these houses. Here is another one. There are three houses like this on the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you put a W by those houses that you think are the direction that the witness was saying.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go then to the next page, page 47.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: For the sake of the record, the witness didn't put a W.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You want a W, sorry. In fact, the wounded when they arrived, they were not taken -- where is the eraser? Okay. In fact, because of the path they came from is this one -- now, it's erased. They went like this, then they crossed. They arrived here. And then that the ones were taken directly to the houses. They didn't go -- they didn't join the main group of prisoners; they were taken directly:

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. President, for catching that. And we would offer this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This marked photo will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P78, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. And, Mr. McCloskey, do you think that this is a convenient time for the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We must have our first break now for technical reasons. We adjourn and resume quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, I think we were still at Sandici meadow at the aerial image of the people, that was 48. Excuse me, that was 46. Now, if we could go to 47. Can you, first of all, tell us who took this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I took this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what does it depict?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This photograph depicts the meadow of Sandici where Humvees are parked in an area that can also be seen very clearly in the video of Mr. Petrovic. Then the little path going up on the left is the one leading to the destroyed houses, the three destroyed houses. The big house is just -- I'm taking this photograph from the two-storage house across the road. And the area marked with yellow is, in fact, the area where on the aerial reconnaissance imagery, we can see the people being sitting. And at the top of it, as you can see, is a slope, and the aerial imagery is taken from the opposite side of it, so this is why on the aerial imagery, it's very difficult to have a real assessment of the size of the terrain occupied by this group of prisoners. This one is a better indication.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So let's go back to 46 to see if we can get an idea. Can you make out anything that looks like a slope in this picture?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. The area --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry, could we just go back to e-court. And this is page 46.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The area that is relatively flat is the area we will mark as being area A. But the area that on the slope that we see in the following picture is this one, B.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So in reality, seen from the ground, the area B is close of being the same size than area A, which is not at all obvious on the aerial imagery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 48 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry, let's admit that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P79, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think that was -- are you sure? Yes. 79. Thank you. Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, we see the same picture we saw on page 47 but with a little insert picture up in the left corner. Can you tell us what this is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, the picture in the frame top left is a still extracted from the video of Zoran Petrovic. One can see men sitting and soldiers standing, and very precise location of this specific event is reproduced on the picture that I took in the yellow box.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How do you know that it's the yellow box where this picture -- that this picture depicts?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: By viewing the film first, and also by identifying, in fact, the -- just the top of the little path that leads, then, if you continue this path, towards the three destroyed houses. The meadow stretching on the right-hand of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So we really need to be playing the video to get that full -- but for the purpose of this testimony, I don't think we'll do that. We have more detail on another witness and another study for Your Honours. Though, of course, we can do anything you choose on that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 49. Now, this is your map with a red dot above Vlasenica and Luke school in blue, which you've talked about before. What is the purpose of this map?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The purpose of this map is to indicate on map the location where the witness was kept prisoner at the school of Luke, claims having been transported on board of a little truck that took him with a group of others from the Luke school, they drove in the direction of Vlasenica, arrived at the level of the soccer field in Vlasenica, they turned left and then they drove for a certain time and distance that was unclear in his testimony in a hilly area so north of Vlasenica that I have roughly indicated on this map because we never found the precise spot, where then he claims having been -- having escaped an execution of those who were inside this little truck. So it's just an indication.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So this red dot is just an approximation roughly describing his description?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: His description that we could not implement with further evidence because we did not find the precise location, though we returned with him but the event for him happened during night-time, and he could be of little assistance in an area where many things look the same. Little hills, little valleys one after another.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's go to page 50 in your book. And do you recall what this photograph is meant to depict?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. This photograph is in connection with the map that appeared very shortly previously and that marked the location of one execution and burial spot that is inside the valley of Cerska. So on this picture seen when taken from the helicopter, the big hill where the men were trapped and trying to cross in the direction of this black arrow, this hill is on the right-hand, so the stretch of road at the right of the picture is at the bottom right, the direction of Nova Kasaba. At the top of it going towards the right around this hill is the direction of Konjevic Polje. And from that point here where the arrow starts is a dirt road that leads inside the so-called valley of Cerska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you there. Let's go back to 50 so we can get a feel for this on the map. We see the red dot near the word Konjevic Polje, and Cerska is a little bit farther down the road; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Konjevic Polje is not the red spot. Konjevic Polje is the little dot that is on -- next to the C of Konjevic, so on the asphalt road. And when we say Konjevic Polje, for the sake of this demonstration, we also talk about the intersection of Konjevic Polje, so a little bit more south than the dot that is on the map. The red dot is the approximate location of the execution burial site we talk about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that is one of the executions that are noted in the indictment, Cerska valley; correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right, then let's go now back to 50, page 51, and I believe that makes a little bit more sense as we orient ourselves. And now let's go to 52. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is a view from the opposite side of the hill. We are always referring to as being the hill from where the people tried then to cross to come towards the direction I'm taking this photograph. And this is the little dirt road that goes to the left, to the inside the valley, and from the hill in front, the search for the Cerska location started with the testimony of a man who said that he saw three buses escorted by APCs entering the valley, so taking this dirt road. And after some time he heard intensive shooting coming from the valley. One excavator entering again this -- now this valley, and then the buses leaving empty, and crossed with another witness testimony of someone who crossed this area by night and at one point shortly after having entered this valley, he was bare foot and claimed having walked in a pool of blood. So this is what sparked the search for possible execution spot in this valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And just to orient ourselves, this roadway we can see going from the right and going from the left, can you tell us the roadway at the base of the hill going to the right, what direction that's going in?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, at the bottom of the hill, this stretch of road goes right towards Nova Kasaba and left towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And then let's -- now I go to the next one, 53.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is the dirt road that will then enter the valley and at one point indeed as the witness claimed, he could not see anymore the buses and the APCs because indeed at one point entering this area, you are completely hidden of sight from the opposite hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 54.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So that's to show that the valley becomes narrow and indeed from the other side, though it's a big hill, it's impossible to see what is going on then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next, 55. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is a suspect area that we ended up finding in this quite long valley, and there are some features on it that I will have to detail then on the following photographs, but this is the spot where the people from the buses were unloaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember why you, as you say, a long valley, why this was a suspect spot?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: In fact, we came to that valley two or three times. The first time was unsuccessful search, so we ended up filming the entire valley. And we had identified a group of three witnesses who didn't know anything about a possible execution in that place, but who spent a week hiding in a little location at Cerska who didn't know how to cross the lines and decided to return towards Srebrenica. And on their way back they hit an area with a very heavy stench that they thought was indeed coming from dead bodies. And at one point of the film, there is a water source that they identified as being close to the location we were looking for, so based on their indications, we returned and found this suspect area. In fact, it was suspect because of this missing soil that I will explain later. And also because of branches that had been put on the side of the road and that had no real reasons to be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Those are the ones we can see on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: On the right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next photograph, 56.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So in this view the end of the valley is in front of us. So the people were coming from the bottom left of the picture, and where the person in blue is standing is the location where the men were lined to be shot and the bodies fell on the slope that we will see -- it's not obvious on this picture, but there is a slope just at the left of the dirt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. As far as you know, were there any survivors to this execution?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: No known survivor on this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you, in the next photographs, explain to us how you came to the conclusion you just made. All right. So let's now go to 57.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is a view of the slope that is just next to the gravel road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what did you do there once you saw this slope, this dirt?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: We dug three holes alongside of this slope in order to check what could be underneath.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
