utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 58. And is that the process of digging you talked about?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. This is the digging process indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And 59.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So in one of these holes we uncovered a group of legs, human legs. It can be seen at the bottom of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 60.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: In the other hole, we uncovered the top of a skull. A human skull.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And 61.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: And in the third one, we can see also a skull and popping out of civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us where this skull is, given that we are not familiar with this sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: At the left of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Right. All right. Now, let's go to 62. We now see a split image screen from this -- again this is US aerial imagery. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So following the discovery of that location, in order to ensure that the event was indeed connected with the July 1995 events and not with anything else, we requested aerial imagery from that precise location. So on the picture at the left dated 5 July 1995, I marked the area where we did this search for a grave in yellow. So one can see there is the gravel road but no additional disturbance. Then compared with 27 July 1995 one can identify two areas of disturbance; one being the left side of the road, so all along the slope we dug; and another one on the right side of the gravel road that we will see on another picture and that matches the soil that the excavator that entered the valley took from the side of the road in order to put the soil on top of the bodies that had been piled up along this edge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 63. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So on this one the markings in the middle show the line, in fact, where the men had to stand. The left side of the picture we are in the process of collecting shell casings. The shell casings were all to be found at the left side of the road, so one can assume that the people were shot at short range and then the bodies fell on the slope. An the arrow on the left indicates the area where fresh soil was taken away to be dumped then on top of the bodies that had fallen on the side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Do you remember at this point roughly how many bodies were exhumed from this grave?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Initially the assumption was that we thought we had to count 50 people by bus, and I think that indeed at the end of the exhumation it was more or less precisely that number that was found.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This might be a good time to talk a little bit about primary and secondary graves. And while you are not an archaeologist, can you briefly tell us about this, how that fit into the investigation and where this grave fit in particular.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: We will talk about the primary and secondary at one point of all this, but this one is a primary since it's the first location where the bodies have been buried, if one can say so. And this one has been untouched. It stayed like this until we finalised the exhumation. It has not been the topic of any further disturbance. Most probably because the number involved was not sufficient to spark a reburial process. 150 victims, unfortunately, in this case, is not a large number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next page, 64. And what is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is -- the red dot marks another burial site near Nova Kasaba, as well as an execution site.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And were there any survivors of these executions?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Not as we know. Only one witness who described the scene and the reason why we tried to find the location, the witness was on the hill, the famous hill we always referred to. And in his line of site in between one pylon and one destroyed house, he witnessed a group of prisoners being taken to a meadow having to line up like for a football match, and from APCs lined along the road, men fired at them. Some time later, a second group came, had to do the same thing, and were shot also. And this witness left the area after a third group suffered the same fate. So we tried to find that spot during a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to page 66. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is the field that we ended up finding. When I say ended up is because we did all the stretch of roads systematically during all the summers we were in the area, and the reason why it took us so long to find is because of this reference, one pylon and one destroyed house. The initial feeling was that they were to be seen in front. In fact, no, they were to be seen from the side. And if I mark the exhibit again with e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You can't. This one is not in e-court. So I think we are okay.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: But one can see at the left of the picture a pylon, and at the bottom left a destroyed house. And in fact this was the angle of sight the witness referred to. So the execution meadow is the one just in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You can mark that now, thank you very much. If you could mark the execution.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The pylon. The house. The field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 67.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we should admit that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P80, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is, unfortunately, a bad quality photograph of the same location, and all the little yellow markings are the ones that were put there by the team that went there with metal detectors in order to pin-point bullets in the ground. So this is the area where these bullets were found in the soil, and that gives an indication of the size, let's say, of this execution field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 68. And what is this in relation to what we've been talking about?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So initially this photograph had only for purpose to show us areas of disturbances in this Nova Kasaba area, so one can see that in these triangles there are two areas of disturbed soil. But this one points with the red rectangle that I have added on the picture the location of this execution field in relation with the disturbances which end up being mass graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right let's go to 69. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is the photograph of -- the top is showing, in fact, where this area of disturbance shown on the aerial photograph is located. So in a corner behind -- close to a tree line. Knowing that -- at the left of the picture is the direction of Konjevic Polje. So it's the direction from where the buses with the deported people were coming from. So it's less chance to be seen also from in this hidden side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Did you go to that area and dig?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 70. Now, it looks like you on the right. Who is on the left?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I'm, indeed, on the right. And the man on the left is John Gerns.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what have you found there?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is a first short exhumation in order to check if there are multiple bodies so that we could qualify the place as being a mass grave. And on this picture, we revealed the presence of six individuals that are, in fact, the first layer of this grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 71. What is this yellow arrow?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is a picture of a man lying with the head towards the soil and with the two arms in his back, and the yellow arrow marks the ligature, that is a rope attaching his wrists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 72.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This one in the same grave, a man wearing a civilian jacket and he also has his arms in the back, and this one is attached with a wire ligature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you make out that wire on the photo?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I think we'll have it clear on the next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 73.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is related to the previous photograph?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It's the same -- more or less the same one, with two markings. One is the marking of the wire ligature, and the other one is his wedding ring. So it shows where the fingers were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 74. We have another red dot. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is a dot to indicate the location of another execution that occurred in this area, and that's the one we call the Jadar river, which is the river that flows in this canyon, in between two steep hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And again, this is your same map that is at scale with each of those squares, 1 kilometre; correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to your next photograph, 75.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: On this one we go back to this hangar at Konjevic Polje which was the end destination for the prisoners who did surrender in the vicinity of 5th Engineer Unit. From this hangar, they were taken on board of a bus. It happened that that day, a random situation there, there was a bus just opposite side of the road. And the red arrow shows the direction that this bus took with these prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let me try to make clear. When did you take this photograph or still?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This one is dated April 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So this bus has nothing to do with anything?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Nothing to do. It's random that a bus appears to be on the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you just used that for your picture, I take it. And the red arrow is to depict what?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The direction the bus with the prisoners on board did take. Along the Jadar river.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that is going in the direction of what major town?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Going -- if one continues this road for about 25, 30 k, it's in the direction of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And let's go to 76.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So Konjevic Polje is at the top left of this picture. This picture is taken from helicopter in order to show what type of terrain it is. In the beginning it's flat, and then you enter really in between two steep hills, and that marks kind of boundary between what we call the area south and the area north. And the arrow points where this bus of prisoners was taken to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 77.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is very close to the spot where the bus made a stop and unloaded the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And why are you going to these places?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Always for the same reason, to try to check all of the ground elements that could either confirm the credibility of the witnesses, either show elements that would make their testimony unreliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, you've used the word "testimony." That's a word we usually associate with people speaking in court under oath. Is that how you mean it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: No, I mean the initial declarations that they gave, first either to the police or the war crime commission, but then that they gave to us as ICTY investigators. And on this occasion, we also brought the witness back to the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And was this a person that said he was survivor?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, he survived the execution. I think he was with a group of 16 people, and they were lined up alongside of the river and shot in the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 78.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So the witness talked about an area where the bus could park and from where they were unloaded and had to walk a little path that led to the river. I mean, not even a path, I mean, an access way to the river. This is a scene from the helicopter, from above, the parking space he referred to. And the arrow marks the direction they took to go towards the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Before picking this particular spot, did you go up and down the road looking for anything else that might look similar to the description?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, because he also in his testimony referred to the fact that when he was floating on the water, he hit the opposite bank and arrived at some barracks that he said were former territorial defence barracks. And, indeed, these barracks exist not far away from, a few hundred metres away from this area. And they became -- after that they became the little bays for the Drina Wolf unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you actually go down to this area and walk it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, the area where he claimed having been shot, we would have it on the next picture, I would guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that's correct. Let's go to 79.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So it's not extremely precisely the place because he was a bit uncertain, let's say, at 10, 20 whatever metres, but our goal was to try to find shell casings in that -- in the place that he did spot, and unfortunately we found nothing, absolutely nothing. But one reason of it could be that the level of the water of this river varies quite considerably, and on one picture we will see the kind of flow that this river might have at spring or God knows when, and that washes things away. That will be the next picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. That's 80.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. So at this moment the river is shallow, but at some point it can carry logs of that size and at that height. So that might be one explanation why we didn't find any shell casing in that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, you have testified today about areas from Srebrenica to Potocari, to Bratunac, up along the road, and did you prepare for this presentation and in the investigation videotape of some of these areas?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I think now that we've had a pretty brief, but, picture of the area that it would be a good time to play his -- these are videos that you yourself took?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I don't know precisely the one that you intend to show, but most probably yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We'll start with the first one that is in the contents of your book, and it's entitled: "Clip Video 1 South to Srebrenica Town."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: 65 ter number 948.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And any questions, please interrupt us. And I probably will ask you some questions. Or just, you can narrate this for us.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this one is again the area south of Srebrenica in order to show the terrain. So the asphalt road here is the road that goes from south to north, so that will at one point reach Srebrenica town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And to remind us the significance of this approach.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That's the area from where the Bosnian Serb army entered the town, but just as kind of a reference because the investigation is not about the military take-over of the enclave; it's about the fate of the prisoners, either military or civilians. So that's Srebrenica town stretched in between the hills. That's the central part of the town where the main mosque used to be. Transformed into a parking-lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you see where the mosque used to be?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it's the yellowish area at the central of this place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we've got some stills on that topic. So we can continue. And what direction are we going now?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Now we are going towards still Srebrenica town, going towards Potocari. And if it continues, then it's the direction of Bratunac. So this is Potocari. These are the factories where the people were taking refuge into, "11 of March" and Energoinvest factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's take a little closer look at this, and --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Sorry, this is the former -- that's the company B, I think, but still in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Tell us what that is.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Can you have it just a few pictures back. Yeah, okay. Yeah. That was the Bravo company which was the bays of the UN battalion inside Srebrenica town, the main bays being at Potocari, for the small bays.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: One can still see the UN markings on the roof, on the left and on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you remember when you shot this video?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I think 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is still Srebrenica town. And after this little stretch of road, just behind this hill is Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. That's the Srebrenica segment. And if we could go to the next segment, which is 984. Should be Potocari.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So more or less in the middle at the left are the factories I thought I did recognise, "11 of March" and Energoinvest. On the opposite is the Express Bus compound, which was an area of regroupment also of refugees. So the two are first factories, and at the right is Express compound. So that was the main area of regroupment of the refugees. One can already see also Express compound, this one close up, "11 of March" and Energoinvest. That was more or less the area of the separation line, here. And I assume I will zoom on the "White House," yeah, in the middle on the left. Yes, the one it's zooming on is the "White House." That is a where the prisoners were taken, once the house was full, they were shipped away towards Bratunac by bus and the process repeated. And this large building is the former accumulator, a battery factory that was, in fact, the main UN base in the safe area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just to be clear, we see to the left a building with a white roof, and then to the right a much bigger building with a partial orange/red roof. Which is the UN? Or both?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The UN base is the one with the reddish roof. The white one was not part, I think, of the UN compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. Now we are heading up towards Bratunac, and so we'll get to 996 as we continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So this is Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 01027. Skipping Kravica section. That was done by someone else, which we'll come back to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's something very different.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We've got the --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: In fact, that's in connection with a big ambush that occurred on the 12. There are still a lot of surface remains to be seen, but it's in combat operation, but that led partially and also led to the surrender process of the 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Tell us about that. What were these just hill-side shots of -- why were you filming that? Based on what did you learn in the investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: In fact, it's an area that confirms, indeed, the fact that as we knew there was a main ambush set up there on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you describe the area for the -- and --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It's on the -- it's the hills. It's along the -- it's on the fleeing path of the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 81 just so that we can get that map up there again to get an idea for the Court where we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We know now that the column left the area of Jaglici/Susnjari, and headed where?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: To the area of Konjevic Polje. So it's on the area we saw on the film, is on the hills behind at the south, the south of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we put this up on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just so you can make just a rough marking where that was, roughly.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It should be somewhere around here. On the precise map of the area, it would be named Kamenica. Which is not to be confused which another Kamenica which is in the Cancari valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When you say Cancari valley, is that in which municipality, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It's in the broad area of Zvornik. It's the area of the crime scenes north. This one we didn't mark? But again, I mean, this area we did not investigate because this was ambush was part of a military operation, so nothing to do with the crimes we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So I should offer this into evidence, this little blip that goes along with the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And when you say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just a question, what does this indicate, this spot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This roughly indicates the location of the ambush of Kamenica and is linked with the short film seen from the helicopter that was spotting, in fact, surface remains. These surface remains are not part of the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P81, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, when you say not part of the case, when this column was going through the woods, and you've already described it partially as an armed head of the 28th Division, were the potential military clashes between that armed column and the Serb forces something you looked into deeply?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The investigation was absolutely not on the fate of the column, aside at the point where the members of this column surrendered or were captured as prisoners. All the rest is linked with a military operation. It was a mixture of armed and unarmed people. The spear-head was mainly composed of the members of the 28th Division. Aside this main ambush that was the legitimate combat operation targeting this column of armed and unarmed people among it, the main military activity took place in the Zvornik area around 15 and 16 when not only did the spear-head go through the lines to try to hit -- to join Nezuk, but also one part of this column did a diversion action, moving -- a large group of them moving towards Zvornik in order to de-route the Bosnian Serb forces from the main objective of the column. But these military aspects were, I mean, useful to comprehend the global process, but they were not at all part of the criminal investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. We should maybe finish up that video that we started that was up in the woods along the path of the column that you were talking about.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: In fact, the aim of this one is then to show the surrender path of those who were being trapped behind these hills, having also suffered this ambush decide on the morning of the 13 to surrender, and then the helicopter will film the way that they took in order reach the asphalt road at the level of Sandici meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that clarification. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we can ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That surface remains. So this is the way going downhill towards the asphalt road, Bratunac Konjevic Polje. Now we take this same road by -- on the ground, no more in helicopter. So that's two-storage [sic] building. Just at the left of the this building is the Sandici meadow, so that's the bottom of the valley where the asphalt road is. And here is that building, so first the men had to go up this path and then walk towards the house. This is the Sandici meadow seen from that house. And on the film of Zoran Petrovic, there are some moments where these angles are nearly exactly the same. So that is the Sandici meadow in 1996. On the other photograph you had cornfields, but at that time there was none. And at the time of the events there were none. And indeed, the first time we went there -- this is a stretcher. We found various items, "licna kartas," clothing, stretchers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what a "licna karta" is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: An identity card. Scattered a bit all over the area. This is the area where the prisoners were sitting on. So that is the area of arrival of the men who surrendered at the asphalt road, and this is all the trail of abandoned items scattering the ground. That's the location from where Zoran Petrovic were filming the people surrendering. That's an example of an ID found on the ground. I don't know what type of ID this was. There's a shell casing. That's a skeleton.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And in your book from pages 77 through 85, you cover some photographs of some individual graves of people near the area of Konjevici. I will skip that, and this will be the subject of another person's testimony. But if we could go to page 86 and start with your discussion of the Kravica warehouse. And can you tell us, give us the briefest synopsis of what the investigation showed happened at the Kravica warehouse on the 13th of July, just to put this in context.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Based on the testimonies of two survivors who had surrendered and been taken to Sandici meadow, both of them were taken to the Kravica warehouse, that is very nearby of Sandici. One by bus taken with a group of others, in total three buses were put in the -- what we named the east part of the warehouse. And another large group was taken by foot and taken into the west part of the Kravica warehouse. And both of them survived the execution that took place inside the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's -- do you know about how many people were executed or were reported executed? The Court will hear much more evidence on this, but just roughly how many people at the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: No, I never wanted to make any rough assessment on this. I only know that there are three buses in one part and that the other part was full, but we do not know precisely how jammed the people were inside. And, no, I would not do any assessment on the numbers, but it was a large number. It is a large warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to page 90 where you first start talking about that. All right, and we have blue and red. Can you tell us what this indicates?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The blue dot is marking the concentration spot of prisoners, and the red dot, the execution site connected with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 91. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a picture taken from the several-storage house just front of the Sandici meadow, and the red arrow points the Kravica warehouse. So it is to indicate that, indeed, it's a very short distance from one place to the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is beyond -- again to try to get us in tune to where we are, what is beyond the warehouse in this picture? What is the next town over?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The next village is Kravica, and continuing in that direction will be Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 92 then.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this again is to show the distance, but this time seen from the air and not the ground. The Sandici meadow is just out of the frame at the bottom of this picture taken from helicopter, and inside the red box is the Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 93. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The blue arrow shows the direction from which the prisoners arrived at the warehouse. And as one can see, this warehouse complex is composed of four buildings, and the one we are interested in is the one alongside of the road, that is in the red rectangle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now can you tell us roughly what sort of warehouse this was in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: In 1995 I would not think it was used for anything because the area was much too dangerous. But in 1996 it was stored for agricultural purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 94. This is a combination shot of -- can you tell us when this winter shot is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So the picture at the top is the first picture that we could take from the warehouse. It was in January 1996 from the ground. The other one at the bottom is dated, I don't know precisely when, but I would think 1998. But the one at the top is the most interesting one since it is the closest in relation to the events. So it shows -- the one at the top shows the entrance, one of the entrance of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is there a significance in the investigation to this broken part?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes. Since the witness who survived inside this west part of the warehouse indicated that once the several waves of executions took place in here, an excavator destroyed part of a wall and entered in order to pick up the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you said that there were people in this west side of the warehouse that were executed. And you mentioned there were two parts. What was the other part?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This west part has two entrances, in fact. This one that is now looking very large, but in fact that was the same size than the one on the left initially. These two ones, they connect with what we call the west part. And then the east part is more at the left of the picture when there is an open space at the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: And another survivor survived from the east part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 95.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is the east part of the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you speak to the survivor of the east part as well?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And let's go to 96. What is the purpose of this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So the picture bottom right is an area reconnaissance imagery showing the Kravica warehouse 13 July, at 1400, approximately. The interest of it is that the witness who survived the execution at the east part of the warehouse said that they arrived by bus. One of the buses, by the way, then did not move any longer because he had been shot in one tire, and on this picture one can see that there are two buses right at the -- one of them being very precisely right at the entrance of the east part of the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And just to be clear on the chronology, the assemble of prisoners on the Sandici field and them being taken to Kravica and shot happened on what day?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: 13 July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next picture, 98. Do you remember what this is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So these are pictures from the inside of the west part of the warehouse. The arrows mark stains that after analysis appear to be human blood-stains.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right, 99.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Same thing. It's a close-up of one of the walls of the west part with blood-stains, human hair, human skin, and explosive residues. But this is inside the forensic report of the full analysis of the Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And that is the subject matter of another witness, who has assembled those forensic reports, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And now let's go to page 100. What is this? It's obvious, but tell us what this is.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a hand-grenade. It was found, I mean, I found it, in fact, in front of the warehouse, just at the edge of the road, so it's a lost grenade. Reason why I nevertheless took the picture is that, according to the survivors, the killing happened by opening fire with automatic weapons from all the openings, but also by throwing grenades inside the building, and aside the grenade handles that we could find just at the bottom of some of these openings, I mean, this is the type of grenade in fact that was thrown inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 101.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So that's one of the grenade handles that were found around the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And 102.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So that's a hole that was most probably done by an RPG rocket firing. An anti-tank rocket fired from one window through the warehouse and exploded at the bottom of the one the walls.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Why do you conclude that, or opine to that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Nothing in reality, because aside from the witnesses -- it's easy to connect the testimonies of the witnesses with the explosions, the grenades since we have the evidence. No one ever talked about someone firing and anti-tank rocket in the building, it's just there, so -- but can I not concluded anything really about this. Knowing also that Kravica village, not the warehouse that is a bit at a distance, but God knows Kravica has been the target of a deadly attack from the 28 division in 1993, and God knows, maybe this thing could be related with another incident, but it's there. And we found also something connected with it in a dump site, but I don't say that it is linked with the event. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right, 103.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That's the exit hole of the explosion, and that shows the direction from where this rocket was fired inside the warehouse. So same line of fire than the ones that were shooting from the windows, but again, I cannot conclude for sure it is connected.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And 104.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is -- it's the west side, and this indicates the area where one of -- the survivor of this execution managed to hide. He said that inside this structure there was what he called a guard house that was a more solid construction, and the first time we went we didn't find it, but because we had only a few minutes for us in the place, but the next picture will show that indeed he said the truth when he said that there was a structure inside this thing.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Because this is where we can see it -- something has been destroyed in that location, and that's the destruction caused most certainly by the excavator that came to collect the bodies. But the marks are very clear, and also the little tiles at the bottom left show that this was some kind of a storage room or whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think it's the break time we've been scheduling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We must have our second break now. And we'll resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, we are still at the Kravica warehouse going over some of your findings as you are at the warehouse. Let's go to 106 in your book. Tell us what this is.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So the first time we could do a decent search of the place, so it was in April 1996, just next to one of the site of the warehouse at the west side in front was a dump site. Going through that dump site of rubbish, soil, and things like this, we could find some samples being - according to anthropologist who was with us, on right of this picture - human bones, and also shell casings, cover of a "licna karta," identity card, a few personal items, broken watch, fake teeth, also and a small metal box for cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 107. What is this for?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this -- this is showing the other side of the warehouse where separate execution took place, and this is the location where the survivor claimed that three buses full of prisoners were taken to this part of the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can we call this the east side?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Absolutely. This is the east side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 108.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a photograph of the inside of the east part of the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, could you make anything of any of the things we are seeing on the wall?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Bullet-holes impacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. How about 109. Let's go to 109.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So 109 is a picture that I took because when the forensics were done in the west part of the warehouse, unfortunately, the east part of the warehouse was unprocessed. So I returned to that location and this specific spot, which is enlarged on the following picture, was a stain, so I collected a sample, and the Dutch lab concluded this was human blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next one, 110.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a closer shot of that sample. And it this was in 1997, since I can read it at the bottom right of the picture. It was in 25th October, 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 111.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The surviving witness said that after when night fell, he jumped off a window at the back of the warehouse. The yellow arrow is pin-pointing the window he claims having jumped from.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 112.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That's a photograph from the back of this warehouse. Again one can see at the right, the last window on the right, this is the one the witness allegedly jumped off, arrived in an area just behind the warehouse. At that time he said there was a cornfield. This picture is dated January 1996, and there is no corn left in winter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But those things we see, the brown debris on the field, were those corn-stalks?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I'm not a botanist, but, yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 113.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this one is a photograph of the window completely at the east of the front of the warehouse, so it's not the window from where the survivor jumped out, but the interesting point is to see that at just underneath this window, the next shot will show it larger, there is a shoe print, and it's a shoe print that is reversed. So it's not the shoe print of someone who is climbing up this window, but it it's shoe print of someone who came from opposite way, from the inside to the outside. So he was not the only one trying to jump out of the window, that's my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 114.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is the close shot of the shoe print.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So I take it, then, the window is above this picture?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Just above this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right, let's go to 115. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a still picture extracted from one of the missing parts of the video that shot Zoran Petrovic when he arrived on the spot with Colonel Borovcanin, the head of the Special Police brigade. If one goes frame by frame through this little piece of a video, this is the door that is at the extreme west of the warehouse from where, as the witness survived inside the warehouse say, that when the fire started people tried to rush out, and obviously they were mowed down at the exit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, can you make out what you think this is in front of this door, these piles?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. It's dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And were you able to review the video like you said over and over again frame by frame to --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And that will come later. That is in evidence, this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go a little further, 116. Can you explain what you are doing here.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So now the goal is to put in relation the pictures of the Zoran Petrovic video and the existing pictures of the warehouse after the events, mainly after this little excavator entered the warehouse, destroying part of this entrance. So in the picture at the bottom left is from January 1996, the destruction is still complete, and in August 1997, part of it has been reconstructed, the top of it. But in reality, the way it has been reconstructed is not exactly the same than initially. There is a distortion of the picture in the film of Zoran Petrovic that makes it look very alike the picture bottom right. But in fact at the time of the events, the door was smaller, because there is also one missing part at the right of this door.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 117.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So again the picture at the top is an extract from the Zoran Petrovic video, and at the bottom right a picture of the warehouse after the events. And in order to see that indeed there is one missing piece at the right, if you compare the three bullet-holes that are in a row at the top and at the bottom of the picture, one can see that at the bottom it is very close to the entrance. And at the top, it's -- there is a missing piece of concrete.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's continue to the next one. This is 118.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is to show how, in fact, these doors were initially in the building, so comparing the lines of the top of the windows and the top of the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But this is of the --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It's the east door of the west part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, so the broken door is to the right of this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The broken door is to the right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Then let's go to the next shot, 119.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this, in fact, now shows the missing parts of the west entrance of the west part of the warehouse. The interest of this being at the final stage to compare the bullet-holes on the walls in order to check if at the time Zoran Petrovic filmed this little piece of footage, the shooting was over or if more holes can be then seen on the facade of the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what conclusion did you make based on your analysis?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The collusions will come with the following picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 120.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: No, the following one, because this one again is to show that on the film, the picture of Zoran Petrovic, the part that is in brown at the right is in fact missing on the pictures that we took from the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. The next one is -- this is 121.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. So now we can compare the picture from the Petrovic video with the pictures of the warehouse, such as it was after the events, at least after January 1996, and the markings show, in fact, where the bullet-holes are on the two pictures at two different dates. One being 13 July, and the one at the bottom being after early 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So those are -- are those matches?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: One will show the difference, the next slide I think shows the difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 122.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So further ones being at the right hand, the three in a row from top to bottom are circled in yellow at the top and also yellow in the picture at the bottom. But there is one additional bullet-hole at the bottom left of these three holes. And even more obvious at the left side, the markings in yellow are the markings that are visible on the two pictures, but in addition to those, they are the bullet-holes marked in red, so three more bullet-holes at the left side at the bottom of this picture. So my conclusion is that, except if one believes that someone later on went and fired for whatever reason on this building, at the time the picture at the top showing the dead bodies was taken, additional shooting occurred after that moment. So the execution in my view, was on-going.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was there any evidence consistent with the shooting on-going after this top video was shot?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: At least it matches the declaration of the person who survived in this part of the warehouse who claims that after the first wave of shooting and grenade explosions, people were called to get out, that the Red Cross was there, so some people got out, and then he heard subsequent shots being fired. And this happened in several waves in fact; the shooting did not occur in one instance, but in several waves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right, and that ends the Kravica warehouse section. So now let's go to page 123, to a new section of an aerial image of Bratunac of 12 July. And can you tell us, these are yellow markings, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: At the end of -- at the end of the day of 13 of July, the prisoners that had been assembled at the soccer field, at Sandici meadow, and various other spots along the road Bratunac-Konjevic Polje, all of these people were taken on board of buses and trucks and transported towards Bratunac, that at the day end of 13 became the main concentration spot for all the prisoners captured during the 12 in Potocari and the 13 both in Potocari and all along the escape routes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's start just briefly with the right side where you've got the football field. What is the significance of that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So the football field, I already talked about it together with the hangar behind the Vuk Karadzic school. These were the places where the first prisoners were taken to. Those captured in Potocari, the 12. And then during the day of the 14 other facilities were used, mainly the Vuk Karadzic school, but also the so-called old school, which is more or less in the same area than Vuk Karadzic school. On another slide we will see that since most of these facilities were probably full, the people had to stay on board of buses and trucks that were parked in several lines in the town. The reference to Hotel Fontana, SDS office is mainly to show that, you know, the centre of the town is -- it's a small town. Not only the authorities, but all the population, everyone knew that this place was at that moment totally packed with prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So the Hotel Fontana indicated here, is that the same place where they had the meetings that's on the famous film?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, this is the location where General Mladic called for a meeting, both the head of UN battalion and Muslim representatives, so it was the first meeting in the evening of the 12th with the UN military and the next day with three Bosniak representatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The SDS office, was there an SDS official that was, and I won't get into the detail of it, but that was involved in these events?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This was the location of the office of the Miroslav Deronjic who was the head of the SDS party for Birac region and who was just after the take-over of the safe area designated by President Karadzic as his special commissioner for Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And lastly you note the Vihor company compound. Do you remember that significance?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It's mainly due to the fact that just in front of the Vihor compound was also a line of buses parked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Right. Let's go to the next one, 124. What are these?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: These are to show, in fact, from the left to the right, from -- it's a panoramic photograph. It's right, it doesn't really look exactly like this because it's close to 300 degree this one. The left is the back of the Vuk Karadzic school, so it gives an indication that it's quite a large building. Just next Vuk Karadzic school, the white wall is in fact the gym, so we have no survivors talking about people being inside the gym, but it would make sense that the gym was also used, since it was in other instances. And in the middle, the hangar, which is the location where the first prisoners were taken to. And totally at the right, the technical school which was also used as a detention facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 125. And this is another US aerial image. And what have you marked there in red and yellow?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The red circle is again the Vuk Karadzic school, the hangar and the old school. In front of the Vuk Karadzic school, the red line represents the location where line of buses and trucks filled with prisoners was parked. More at the bottom of the picture is another red line representing the same thing, the location of the line of buses filled with people. And totally at the top is also a factory which was in fact the HQ of Bratunac Brigade. And in front of this location was also a line of buses and trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've already told us that the black and white on these photographs was information provided by the US, the coloured information that you put in. We notice that there's a little white box below the bigger box that's blank. Do you recall what, if anything, you did with that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I blanked it because I used only the imagery support as showing Bratunac town, not to make this picture say anything else than this is Bratunac. The markings are done by myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go -- now we start to get into, I believe, what you call executions area north. And this is your first map, so can you tell us about what this depicts?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Starting in the night of 13 to 14, so in fact, the very early hours of 14 of July, the evacuation of all the prisoners who were packed in Bratunac town started. The first line of buses with prisoners took the direction of the north towards Zvornik and brought the prisoners to a school at the location named Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's not real clear, but is that what is marked in yellow?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Let me see. Yes. But, in fact, the name of the school is -- I have a memory hole.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 127 in your book.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Grbavci. The Grbavci school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So we have an aerial image. And can you tell us, what is this information of these areas north basically based on? I don't want to reconstruct the entire investigation in these matters, but let's say for Orahovac, for example, how are you getting this information to go and take pictures?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The identification of this precise location came during the summer 1995 where according to the witness who was taken to -- we are looking in an area close to Zvornik for a school that had a gym attached to it and that was close to a railroad, since the execution spot is very nearby and was just next to a railroad. So, in fact, we ended up finding such a map, and apparently the only school with a gym close to a railroad line was this one. So the intention was to go to the school, check if the description of it matched the description of the witnesses, and then also find the execution sites, and find the mass grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And let's go to 128. Split image, what is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So it's a split image that makes, in fact, one image. If someone is just at the entrance that leads from the school which is at the right to the gym. The witness said that they had to drop their bags in front of it and then walk along a fence - the fence is the thing that you can see in the middle of this path - that led to a door, and from that door they could enter the gym, which is indeed the way one enters this place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 129.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So the door in the middle is the door from where someone enters this gym. The prisoners were sitting on the floor, and after some time they were taken, in fact, one by one entering this little wardrobe, the arrow exit, given a sip of water, being blindfolded and then getting on board of a little TAM truck waiting for them outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know when this photo was taken? I think the last one had snow.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This was taken later. This one was taken either 1997 or even 1998. In 1998. This one was taken in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 130.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That one was taken in 1996. According to those who were inside this gym, from time to time when they were a bit talking too much, bothering, making a bit of noise in the gym, the guards were shooting a few rounds in the air. So this is a bullet-hole in ceiling of the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 131.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That's another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's a different location.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, that's a different location of the roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And 132.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So these are pictures of the windows in order to check if they match the description made by the people who were inside. So that's one of the walls.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, 133.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: These are also holes in the windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did these windows match anything that any of the witnesses said?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. And we later on brought them also back to the place in order to ensure and give -- and receive more details.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall how many survivors you identified in the investigation of the Orahovac case?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I think four.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 134 now. Do you know roughly when this photograph was shot?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, that was April 1996. It's 11 April 1996. It's at the bottom right of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So two things on this one, again one can see the fence at the back of this playground which is the fence one of the survivor talked about when he said, That's where we entered the gym. And on the left, top left, it's the door from where the people were taken out. And the TAM truck was parked in front of this one. And just in front is a pile of rubbish, of rubbish, and we went through a search of this pile of rubbish.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, the door you are talking about the people went out, can you describe so we can see it from -- just where is it in this picture?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It's at the top left. It's the one that has a fence on it, but the fence was -- I mean, can be open. And there is a destroyed blue half door and the little few stairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall that doorway changing at all as you visited this place over the years?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: After two years it was sealed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 135. And what is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So these are the items that we discovered when we went through the pile of rubbish. So mainly shell casings of various calibres, but most important of it is the large number and the various types of blind -- of pieces of cloth looking as blindfolds that we could take away from there and later on compare with blindfolds that were found in the mass graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And was that comparison done?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that's subject to another expert report?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 136.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So again it's photographed samples of pieces of cloth and also of ligatures attached to a piece of a track, either a bulldozer or tank track.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And let's go to 137.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So again these are pieces of cloth that we seised and brought back as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That's the exit door, but at the time it was later sealed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right, 139.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So on this picture, well, two things, at the bottom left, bottom left is the direction of Grbavci school. So continuing, in fact, north, one path is the road, and at the left of the road is the railroad. And where the arrow points, execution site 2, in fact, there is a path that turns left, then there is a dirt road that goes through a very small tunnel underneath the railroad line, and then it turns right and it hits an area behind the railroad. So the first persons who were -- the first trucks who were bringing the people to the execution site went through the site once. They went first under the railroad line, and then behind it was the first execution site.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's look at another aerial image, 140. We see two different dates on this. What is the significance? Can you try to orient us on this. This seems a little strange.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So again, let's take first the picture dated 5 July. At the left, the line is the asphalt road that at the top goes towards the Grbavci school. So coming from the top of the picture, one should turn first to the left where it is written "1995," continue a little bit, pass under the straight line that is the railroad, then go under the railroad, turn then towards the right, and at the bottom right of the picture is the area of the execution field. When compared with the picture dated 27 July 1995, one can notice two areas of disturbance. One at the location that I just mentioned, the bottom right of the picture where it's now visible, the large area, white area which is disturbed soil, and that, in fact, corresponds to the area of the mass grave. And once this execution site was totally covered with bodies, one of the survivors recalls that the execution team leader said take the ammunition box, and we go to the other side. And the other side is, in fact, opposite of the railroad, very close to the asphalt road, and this is the area of disturbance that you can see between the top of the picture and where written 27 July. There's an area of disturbance that you do not have on the picture dated 5 July, and where also we later on found a mass grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Those two mass graves you just have briefly referred to that we can see on these two areas of disturbed earth, and just -- were they determined to be primary graves or secondary graves?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: These ones are primary graves. People were buried on the spot of their execution. The burial of the people at the first site was even, according to the survivors, on-going, meanwhile the execution was also on-going.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did the forensics reveal that these were undisturbed primary graves like Cerska or something else?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: These ones were later severely disturbed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right, so we'll get into that a bit later. Let's go to 141.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So, in fact, this is the same picture than the previous one, but I added the yellow markings on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And now let's go to 142. What does the LZ-2 mean?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is in fact -- this is a picture taken from the railroad that is on quite high elevation, and that gives a view on the execution field, with where the arrow points one can see an area of disturbance, which is the same disturbance that one could see on the aerial imagery. And from the little tree line at the right and where the plants are and the forest, this was the total size of the execution spot. And at the left side of the picture, at the left side of the yellow arrow, was the area where, in fact, the executioners were staying. It was the so-called rest area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 143.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is the terrain when we first arrived on it, and the little markers, they spot various things that we could see on the surface of the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's too far from us for us to be able to see. We'll get into that a little later.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: There are close shots, a few samples of it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Again, do you remember the month and year that this photo was taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: April 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 144. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So label 25, human bone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how do you know that was human?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Because it was the assessment of the anthropologist Bill Haglund who was together with us on this mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And 145.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That's a jaw.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Human jaw?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Human jaw.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Shell casing.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: A piece of cloth and also a ligature. A piece of cloth with a knot, and above it it's another piece of cloth, but it's still embedded in the ground; it's a piece of clothing in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right, 148. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Seventeen is the location of a shell casing, and 43 shows the distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And 149.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this one is the so-called rest area on which we found no bones, no clothing, nothing, but a few things that still connect to the execution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 150, then.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So these are pieces of boxes in which the ammunition is packed, the cartridges are packed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry, could we go back to 149. Just over the -- as we look at this, the left side of this white vehicle, what is that? That structure.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That is the little bridge of the railroad under which one has to pass in order to come from the Grbavci school to this precise location. So it's hidden from road by the elevation of the railroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 151.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That's a metal box that was found in this position but that appeared to be an ammunition box.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Where in relation to this area is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: If you take the picture before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, let's do that.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: No, the one before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Next one.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: At the top, at the top of this little slope, just behind the first bushes, was obviously thrown there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go back to 151, then. And did that have anything do with the investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: One could think so, since, as I said previously, one survivor overheard the leader of this little squad saying, Take the ammunition box and we move to the other side. This ammunition box was already empty. We found this little subpackaging scattered on this so-called rest area, so as we will see on the next picture, I think such a box contains 1.200 rounds, so at least one of these boxes was already used.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 152.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is what is written on the box. It's 7.62 calibre ammunition, and, indeed, I think it's 1.280 rounds in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's the same box, you've just turned it around so you could read it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, 153.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this photograph is only designed to show how the packaging of ammunition is made. This box was discovered in a very different location. We were looking, in fact, for bodies in a cave, and we found a hiding place for ammunition. So it's in fact, a wooden box, and inside this wooden box is a metal box of the same type that -- of the one we found at that execution site. And inside of it are these little subpackaging boxes that contain each of them, I don't know, maybe 10 cartridges.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 154.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is a view seen from this execution and burial site that shows the direction then to go not only towards the Grbavci school but to the next execution site which is Lazete 1. The reason why we labelled LZ-1 and LZ-2 is, in fact, a mistake. Based on the assumption that the first execution site, logically, was the one close to the road, and then the second one, LZ-2, the one that we have here in front. But in reality it was totally reversed, but we couldn't know that at the time. The first execution site is this one, the LZ-2. LZ-1 is the last one, the second one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Where did you come up with in word "Lazete"?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That was the name that was on the maps we used in 1995 and 1996, but later on we had other maps naming this area Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 155.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So again now, picture taken from the railroad elevation but looking to the opposite direction, so towards the asphalt road that, to the right, leads to the Grbavci school. And the area that I circled in yellow is the area of disturbance, so both execution and burial site.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 156.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is to put in relation these two sites. So again, the arrow shows the direction of the trucks bringing the prisoners. Then turning left, going under the railroad line, the triangle being the first execution site, LZ-2, and burial site. And then the last site here was LZ-1.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We don't see any crime scene photographs of LZ-1. Do you recall if there was any indications of any execution going on there that you found on the ground at the time?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It was a very, very difficult location to search because when they opened the mass grave to create the mass grave, they severed a pipe, and all this terrain was totally flushed with water, and so it was extremely muddy and hard to try to find anything. We probed the place with an auger also, that indeed revealed that there was dead bodies in that place. I mean, the soil had been contaminated by human flesh, but it's the exhumation then that brought out the evidence from this place, not the surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 157. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a garbage place, very close by to the execution site. The other photograph will show it. So we went again in detail through this garbage and could find a number of items of interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 158.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So that's the beginning of the lineup of what we were finding. In fact, we were finding hats, pieces of clothing, and again, a large number of pieces of cloth, blindfold style.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When you say hats, anything particular about the hats you found? What kind of hats?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The type of hats that old men wear in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 159. Just -- we see a big yellow "dump site."

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, so in fact that once under the railroad line turning right it goes to the execution site. But if you continue going a little bit up and then turning left, it's something like 100 metres, is the -- on the site of the path is the dump site that we searched.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's now leave Orahovac and go to the next one, 160. This -- we see that you have the yellow marking next to the village of Petkovci?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And the Judges have not yet heard any evidence on this, so can you tell us about this.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. The same day, 14 July, another convoy of prisoners was headed towards Zvornik, past Zvornik and were taken to a school named Petkovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we can see Orahovac below that, if we squint. So this --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It's more north than Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And do you recall, were there any survivors to Petkovci?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: There were could survivors from the execution site connected with the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And can you describe your investigation, what it revealed? Let's go by your photographs as we've been doing. 161.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So again this is a view of the school taken from helicopter. It shows the distance from the road. It's a two-storage building.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And was this consistent with any description you received?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Not this side, but the other side. Because this seems a high construction and -- in fact, when you approach it. But from the back, you have to go down then stairs in order to hit the entrance. The photographs all, I mean, match the description of the approach, the inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 162.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So that's a view from the front. The reason why it was taken is that there were guards in front, and in the field, in front of the school. And when some prisoners were trying to stand up in order to get some fresh air at the windows, apparently what is said is that they were shooting at them so that they stay sitting down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
