utterances.text: And when you say front, in which direction is this from the road we just saw on the previous?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The road is in the back of the one who took the picture, and I think I took this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Can you just -- so is the person -- where is -- from 162 where is the road?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The road is at the back of the person looking at this picture, in the back. Just 10 metres behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So the back of the person that took the picture?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 163. Is this the same a place?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yeah, this is the same place but seen from the back. The asphalt road is bottom -- top right of the picture, goes on to the right towards the -- I mean, goes to the left towards the dam.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So is this the other side of the school --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The other side, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And let's go to 164.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is the entrance with stairs going down, as described by the survivors, they were walking in between two lines of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what did they describe, when you say going down?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: They describe the approach of the school. They described going up -- the one I interviewed at least, because I didn't -- I interview one, and another colleague interviewed the other one to make sure we were not under the influence of one or the other. And the one I interviewed then took a staircase inside, then a corridor, and was put in a classroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 165. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That shows the ground floor and the first floor, the staircase being at the right of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, 166.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That's the staircase.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That's the corridor, and he was at the last classroom at the right.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So he described that there was a stove, a few details that match what we could find inside, though at the time we went, part of it had been renovated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, 169. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is the blackboard of the classroom, and the markings on the board are bullet-holes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Why did you note those?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: In order to potentially, I say potentially, confirm the fact that there was shooting coming from the outside to the inside, as described by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, 170.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That is a closer shot of the board.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you've got 171.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That's the exit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And 172.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Again, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, I've overlooked offering the videos, short videos into evidence at the time, as I'm required to do so. So perhaps I can do that now. They were 948, 984, 996, and 1027.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: They all will be received as separate videos -- separate exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 948 will be Exhibit P82; 984 will be Exhibit P83; 996 will be Exhibit P84; 01027 will be Exhibit P85, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. That finishes the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 173. We see you've got a mark that is still near Petkovci. Where are we going now?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The prisoners who were inside the school of Petkovci were taken out, put on board of trucks, and driven to a nearby location, that is the dam of Petkovci. The dam of Petkovci being, in fact, a reservoir of liquid pumped from a nearby aluminum factory. So it's chemical waste dam, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 174. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: At the middle right, the path is the access path that leads to this large area which is the plateau at the foot of the dam, and this is the area where the trucks were ending, the people were unloaded, and this is, in fact, the execution area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And let's go to 175. This is -- you've chosen to put this here. Again we are at these US aerial images. Can you tell us what this signifies?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I should have pointed on the previous picture an area of disturbance where the people are. In fact, we make, more or less, the tour of this area of disturbance, and this is the photo shown -- a comparison shown on the next one, which indeed pin points the area of disturbance, which will, in fact, be more relevant when we talk about the disturbance of the graves because, in fact, the one of 7 September 1995, the disturbance already exists, but at the time the belief was that this place, based on the imagery, had not been disturbed, but we knew it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, you said that there's this water dam. Is there any water on this? And this is hard for anybody to make out, unless you've been there. Can you tell us where this is in relation to the water that you spoke of?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yeah, this is in fact, the plateau of a dam, so the foot of the dam, and then at the right side of the picture will be the wall of the dam, and completely right would be the red lake of aluminum chemical waste.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: But we will see it on another picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 176.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is another view of the execution area, so the plateau of the dam. The little picture on top of it is a picture that I took of one of the two survivors, and he indicated me that day where he was standing because when he arrived there, the executioners told him to find a free spot. The place was covered with bodies. And the arrow marks the location where he told me that he stand there. In front is a little hill with a wood which will be of relevance, because the escapeway for him and his companion who was very nearby him also was first to crawl into some ditch, then hide into a small forest from where they could see what was going on, on the dam. And then their escape route was to go uphill towards the left of this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 177. What is the significance here?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That is the ditch that was described by the survivors as the ditch in which he first entered before hitting the little forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right, and 178.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So here you have the picture we were talking about. You recognise the plateau, the execution area and burial area. Then more at the bottom still in white, it's the wall of the dam. And in orange, which is the natural colour of the water, is, in fact, the lake. And the marking in blue is the escape route of the two survivors.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can't see the clock from here, but I'm told it's time to quit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Absolutely correct. You are running out of time, and we have to adjourn for the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I can tell you that I should finish before the end of tomorrow, so I would think there should be some time for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We have to adjourn for the day, and we will resume tomorrow in the afternoon in courtroom 3 at 2.15. I think you are fully aware of your situation, you have to stay and come back to the court tomorrow. Thank you very much. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
